title: FatterDarr
tagline: It checks nobody's watching before swapping a file for a smaller copy.
what: A work queue for the roughly 34,000 video files on my home server. One at a time, the graphics card in my gaming PC re-saves each file in a smaller format and puts it back, so the same library takes up less disk.
built: Wrote the queue server and the graphics-card worker that replaced the ready-made tool I ran before
Added a guard that asks my media server if anyone is watching before a file gets swapped
Set aside any file that fails three times, and taught it real errors from files that won't shrink
Tuned the network reads that feed the graphics-card worker
Made new movies show up in Recently Added as soon as they land
credit: Wrote it myself, to replace Tdarr, the ready-made tool it took over from

making.problem: I wanted a smaller video library without interrupting a movie or making the queue retry the same file forever.
how: A small server keeps the queue and one row for every file.
A worker on my gaming PC does the encoding on the graphics card and reports back live.
Before replacing a file, the worker asks Jellyfin, my media server, whether anyone is watching it.

broke.title: A key just for the viewer check
broke.body: The viewer check lost access after a server move. I gave it its own sign-in key, so changing my password cannot break it.

log.text: Ran the queue, graphics-card worker and file replacement end to end.
Gave the viewer check its own sign-in key.
Separated videos that cannot shrink from files with read errors.
Raised network read speed from 32 to 70 MB/s to keep the worker fed.

serviceRecord.purpose: Make the same movie library take less disk. A queue feeds the graphics card one file at a time and checks for viewers before a swap.

receipt.title: New means new.
receipt.text: A newly imported movie appeared in Recently Added with the right arrival date. I made the importer stamp the arrival and notify the library, rather than wait for a later scan.

serviceRecord.care: Check for viewers before replacing a file. Put repeat failures aside so the rest of the queue can move.

entries.text: Ran the queue, graphics-card worker and file replacement end to end.
Separated videos that cannot shrink from files with read errors.
Raised network read speed from 32 to 70 MB/s to keep the worker fed.

back.pitch: A smaller video library without interrupting movie night. My queue sends files to the gaming PC to be re-saved, then checks nobody is watching before replacing them.
cut: Three failed attempts put a file aside instead of retrying forever.
Import notifications that put new arrivals into the library.
